newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gentech buys Stantronic for 84.5 mln rand.
newsitem.headline: Gentech buys Stantronic for 84.5 mln rand.

text.p: General Technologies Ltd (Gentech) on Thursday announced it had acquired Stantronic for 84.5 million rand with effect from March 1, 1997.
The consideration will be discharged by Gentech issuing new ordinary shares at an issue price of 13.2 cents per share to Stantronic shareholders.
In addition, Gentech will undergo a change of control and change its name to Stantronic Group Holdings Ltd.

This will take place with Power Technologies Ltd (Powertech), through its wholly-owned subsidiary Gentech Holdings, selling its 53.5 percent shareholding in Gentech to the controlling shareholders of Stantronic, represented by Gary Abrahamson.
The transaction will take effect from March 1, 1997 and Gentech Holdings will receive about 4.2 million rand for its 30.4 million shares in Gentech, equivalent to 13.9 cents per share.

As a result of the proposed change of control together with the Stantronic acquisition, the Gentech business will change to that of a company holding interests in the electrical contracting and maintenance, lighting design and commercial refrigeration industries.

In terms of the change of control and acquisition, Abrahamson and the controlling consortium will directly and indirectly control 75 percent of Gentech and will make an offer to minorities to sell all or part of their shares to Abrahamson at 13.9 cents per share.

But Gentech cautioned that this price was related to the group's position prior to a proposed capital restructure and advised shareholders to await full particulars of the financial effects of the recent transactions which would be detailed in a circular within 30 days.
Gentech said it planned to consolidate its share capital on a five-to-one basis.
In anticipation of the deal, Gentech's share price moved sharply on Tuesday, dropping to a new year low of 32 cents in volumes of more than 1.6 million shares.
